A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B. Existing content can be matched reliably across pagination and table renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, finetuning experiments, and controlled ablations in Tables 1–7 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds EVA-CLIP evaluations and MMVP/MMVP-VLM prompt-ablation results.

M1.justification: The token-processing adaptations, RoPE, VLM2Vec conversion, training objectives, and M3ID decoding procedure are unchanged. The additions evaluate existing procedures without introducing a method component.

E1.justification: The LCS-558K/DataMix-665K training data and evaluation benchmark suite are retained. MMVP and MMVP-VLM already appear in v2; the new prompt ablation uses their existing content without changing the underlying matching task.

E2.justification: v3 adds EVA01-ViT-g-14, called EVA-CLIP in Table 4, to the Table 3 benchmark comparison and Table 4 finetuning comparisons. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4 adds evaluation using original MMVP questions and manually written MMVP-like questions for MMVP-VLM, with a no-question control and no reported prompt tuning. Existing evaluation metrics, sample counts, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The question-removal ablation previously reported on What’sUp in Table 7 is extended to MMVP and MMVP-VLM in new Table 11. Table 4 also extends the finetuning and hard-negative analysis to EVA-CLIP. Earlier analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the experimental results. Added results follow the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All matched existing table entries remain unchanged. v3 adds EVA-CLIP results in Tables 3–4 and Table 11 reports VLM2Vec pair accuracies of 30.0/37.8 on MMVP/MMVP-VLM, versus 9.3/11.9 without questions and 14.0/20.7 for CLIP.

T1.justification: The PACL weighting equations, SPARC construction, and M3ID correction rule are unchanged. No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about extracting information from a shared vision encoder, architectural factors, and the sufficiency of contrastive finetuning. The new experiments provide additional support for those claims.

C2.justification: The question-based reweighting explanation, interpretations of unsuccessful finetuning, and limitations in Section 6 and Appendix B.6 remain unchanged. Appendix A.4 adds cross-benchmark support for the existing prompt interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project code link on the first page and documents EVA-CLIP’s checkpoint provenance, evaluation implementation, and finetuning settings. Appendix A.4 explains the new question construction and states that the questions accompany updated supplementary material.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to EVA-CLIP by Sun et al. (2023) and LAION-400M by Schuhmann et al. (2021) for the added baseline and its provenance. The substantive research positioning in Section 4 is retained.

P1.justification: There are limited wording and grammar edits, clarification that the LLM2CLIP footnote concerns the original model, and updated funding acknowledgments. The section hierarchy and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 3–4 gain EVA-CLIP rows and new Table 11 displays the prompt ablation. Figure 2’s caption is expanded and Table 10’s caption identifies response-based evaluation. The three figure graphics are unchanged; subsequent appendix tables are renumbered and reflowed.

improvement.justification: The added EVA-CLIP comparisons and Table 11 prompt ablation modestly strengthen the evidence, particularly by testing question dependence beyond What’sUp. The project code link and additional setup information improve reproducibility guidance. These are useful extensions to an otherwise stable paper whose original results and methodological limitations remain.
